name: Dispatch and command traffic
description: The responders' view of dispatch: CAD incident detail, unit status board, pending calls, radio traffic across dispatch, command and tactical channels, station alerting and mutual aid requests, with the decisions of mutual aid, command transfer and a mayday. The 911 center's own view and CAD failure stay with the emergency communications domain.
outsideParties: gas, electric and water utilities on call

advisorRoles.name: Dispatch Supervisor
advisorRoles.description: Owns call load, unit moves between districts, the whiteboard and the decision to request mutual aid.

advisorRoles.name: Communications Unit Leader
advisorRoles.description: Owns the incident radio plan, channel assignments and interoperability.

decisionForms.label: Call for mutual aid or state resources
decisionForms.description: Ask another agency or the state for units, with what, how many and where they report.

decisionForms.label: Transfer command
decisionForms.description: Command passes from one officer to another with a briefing, and the change is announced.

decisionForms.label: Declare a mayday
decisionForms.description: A responder calls for help; command clears the channel and starts the rescue and accountability.

glossary.definition: Computer-aided dispatch: the record of a call and the status of each unit, with times for dispatched, en route, on scene, patient contact, transporting and at hospital.
The alert sent to a station for a call, with text on the station printer and a spoken announcement.
Available, dispatched, en route, on scene, patient contact, transporting, at hospital, committed or out of service.
Emergency traffic from a responder in trouble. Command clears the channel and starts rescue and an accountability report.
Personnel accountability report: every company confirms its members are accounted for.
A printed list of the units that respond to each call type and address, used when CAD is down.

productConventions: A CAD incident detail lists units with the time of each status change; a unit does not show a later time without the earlier ones.
The radio traffic log gives time, channel, from, to and the words spoken, in plain language. Emergency traffic is flagged in words.
A mutual aid request names what, how many, where to report and who authorized it.
Times are 24-hour; CAD numbers look like CAD 26-104417.
realismRules: Plain language on the radio: no codes that another agency would not know.
The status board, the CAD detail and the radio traffic agree on which unit is where and when.
A mayday is announced three times, command clears the channel, and an accountability report follows.
A command transfer names who gives command, who takes it, the time and a briefing, and is announced.
A surge leaves calls waiting: pending calls grow, mutual aid answers take minutes, and a district can be left uncovered.
This toolkit shows the responders' view; the 911 center's own CAD failure belongs to the emergency communications domain.
